about: Engine knobs, one row each, keyed by engine, and how `boltbeam tune MODEL --engine E` sets them on the machine it runs on (workflow/tune.py reads it, with each engine's adapter module from engine_adapters.json). kind: env (an environment variable), flag (a command-line flag), switch (a flag that takes no value: on puts it on the command, off leaves it out), config (a key of a JSON config flag, a.b). requires: the build features the knob needs (the adapter's detect: llama.cpp the getenv names compiled into the build, vLLM the flags its installed arg parser adds and the Literal values of its config classes); a row whose feature is missing is not in that build. group: the engine's named extra the knob comes from (an arkey_ie_mods mod: the group row names it, the shipped index its marker in any version; workflow/mods), for the words. applies: an expression over facts. derive: facts (a formula, instant), measured (a short real-text prefill sweep under --measure, over the row's axis knob, or a choice: decode speed at tune.SERVED requests at a time on real-text prompts over a candidate list fact, kept only by core/draft_count's paired rule and, with gate agreement, only past Speed up's next-token agreement gate at the setup's context; without --measure the facts value or the default stands, said so), default (left at the default, with the evidence why). bitwise false: the knob changes outputs (said beside it); output, output_why: for such a knob, what stands behind a value that is not bitwise: quality-gated (tune keeps it only past its agreement gate) or untested (workflow/context_audit.output_label; row_output states the default once). audit_flags: engine flags `tune` does not move, kept for the long-context audit (workflow/context_audit.py): names (the flags of one setting), role (what the audit reads it as), output and output_why as above, log (the patterns of the engine's own log lines, named groups); switches (flags of the row that take no value); bitwise, as a knob's. output_from: the fact that holds a derived value's own label (<fact>_why its evidence), read only when the value is that derived fact's (the same name less _output); else output stands. aliases: a knob's other spellings. output_neutral: the flags whose value cannot change one request's answers, per engine; every other flag a run recorded is judged by a row or reads unjudged; an expression over value says when. with: the flags a flag row goes with ({value} and facts filled in); with_draft: those for the draft model, only when the command loads one. output_check false: the output check cannot see the row's effect (its tool does not run what the row changes), so a check that differs in it is refused (tune.unchecked), and the row takes no agreement gate. vram: the GPU memory a row's subject takes at a value (value None: its default), a formula over the facts, its terms and value; the rows that declare it are chosen together by workflow/tune.memory_fit, from one budget: engines.<E>.after_load (the engine's estimate of the GPU memory free once the model is loaded, terms and a formula, read as gpu_after_load_bytes and load.<term>) plus what the rows take at their defaults, less a margin for what a session adds after load. fit: the row's values for that fit (candidates: a list, or a formula over the facts; a sweep's keep rule applies) and, optionally, gain: its predicted speed over its default at a value, a formula, and gain_words, where that came from; a combination that changes the answers counts only past the output check (--measure). default_from: the fact that holds the default the build states (its --help), in place of default. measured_with: rows whose defaults the value was measured with; a setup that sets one says so beside it. Formulas use only the facts in workflow/tune.FACTS and the adapter's namespaced facts (ns.name), numbers, strings, + - * / //, comparisons, and/or/not, x if c else y, min, max, pow2_floor, gib_floor, gib_ceil, floor_to. placed true: the row hangs only on where the experts sit and on RAM (the adapter's placed_facts), so the offload page states it beside each placement's flags (tune.placed); needs: what such a row says when the build was not read. measured_when/measured: a clause of measured numbers a row adds to its reason only when the expression is true over this run's facts (the setup it was measured in), so a general reason never quotes another setup's numbers. Adding a knob is adding a row; adding an engine is a row under engines, its knobs and an adapter module.

thinking.about: How tune knows a model thinks, for the --reasoning-budget and -bs rows (tune_llama_cpp.thinking_facts): the chat template (a --chat-template-file or a Jinja --chat-template given through --flags, else the GGUF's, template_key) names one of the end-of-thinking tags llama.cpp's chat parsers end thinking at. llama-server applies a thinking budget only where it finds the template's thinking tags, so a model without them gets no flag; a template that builds its tag from pieces reads as not thinking (the flag is then left off, said). budget: the knob row it gates; --flags giving it keeps the command's own value
thinking.builtin: a built-in template's name: its text is not read here, so the GGUF header's template stands for it
thinking.why_none: the model's chat template names no end-of-thinking tag ({tags}), so llama-server applies no thinking budget to it
thinking.why_flags: --flags give it ({value}): the command's own value stands

after_load.formula: (gpu_free_bytes - llama_cpp.on_card_bytes - llama_cpp.kv_cache_bytes - gpu_count * (t.compute_buffer_bytes + t.context_buffer_bytes + t.server_bytes)) * gpu_free_min_bytes / max(gpu_free_bytes, 1)
after_load.evidence: the GPU's free memory now (NVML's: the driver's own reserve, 497 MiB on the RTX 5090, is not in it) less the model's weights on the card, the KV cache llama.cpp allocates at the context (tune_llama_cpp.load_facts: the attended layers' K and V and a sparse indexer's keys at the command's type, a quantized type's dequant copy, each slot's recurrent state), the compute buffer (the chunk's expert activations, an estimate from the model's shapes, plus a term per cell and chunk token: the f16 attention mask, 2 bytes, and for a k-pool indexer its scores and selection masks, 7.7 bytes measured) and what llama-server takes beyond its own buffers (CUDA context, cuBLAS, what CUDA's free figure holds back: 705 MiB on the measured chip). That runtime and the stock k-pool masks are rows of data/machine_figures.json keyed by chip (server_runtime, kpool_mask); a chip with no row borrows the nearest, widened by its readings' spread, and tune says so. Measured 2026-11-17 on the RTX 5090, b11571 (~/storage/tmp/rel27/fit): llama-server's own fit projection at -c 16,384 to 247,552, -ub 512 and 1024, f16 and q8_0 (Flash-Next IQ1_M: compute grows 3,943 bytes per cell at -ub 512 and 7,814 at -ub 1024 in f16, the same plus 2,048 in q8_0; Qwen3-14B and Qwen3.8-27B: 1,024 and 2,048, the mask alone), and two loads (-c 65,536 all experts on the GPU, -c 247,552 with llama.cpp's own -fit placing 7 layers' experts in RAM): NVML's free memory before the start less the logged model, context and compute buffers less the free memory CUDA reported after load was 704 and 706 MiB; the estimate lands within 25 MiB of the projection at 65,536 and 247,552 cells. The earlier 1.7 GiB runtime (2026-11-11) absorbed the per-cell terms this formula did not have. The streamer's slot count, the memory fit and the Recommended setup's context read it. Several cards: llama.cpp splits the layers (weights, KV) by each card's free memory and holds a compute buffer and a runtime on each, so the estimate is the tightest card's share; a cost that does not split (the draft head, the sampler) must fit there, and each card streams with its own slots. The -ctk row's cost is charged likewise: the model's KV at the tightest card's share, the draft head's whole (one card holds the head). The runtime and the per-cell terms are CUDA readings; another vendor's are not measured

spend.about: The spend fit's rows (workflow/spend.py): each way a llama.cpp command trades GPU memory for speed or context. read: how a command sets it (flags: an integer flag and its default; env: a switch, on at its on value, or with no on value the count it is set to; file_flags: a file the adapter reads a fact from, spend_value); bytes: the memory it takes at a value (a formula over the facts; spend.<row> is each row's value in the combination, load.<term> the engine's after-load terms at the combination's sets); moves: the session metrics it can move (step_ms, prefill_ms, tokens_per_step), each taken only from a measured unit (a session-ab arm or a measured row) whose rows are the combination's; requires: the getenv name the build must have; built false: no switch exists yet (shown with what it would free, never chosen); on: the value a pending row would take; values: the row's own values; fit_value {min, step}: each combination takes the largest value it fits (none behind an expert cache); only_where_default_fails: another value only where the same combination at the default holds less context; valid: when a combination is legal (context_tokens: the cells it holds); range: a count fact whose 0..N are the row's values. sink: the row whose layers in RAM get the expert cache, which takes whatever is left. cell_bytes: what one more cell of context takes (main and draft). argv_facts: other values read from the measured command. headroom: what a session can add after its lowest (new and resumed prompts), kept free by every fit: the first row the build has (requires, built), kind bound (its bytes formula over its params: inline, from its record, or formulas over the combination) or mitigation (the most any stored or given stress of the model grew).
spend.cell_bytes: load.context_buffer_bytes / context_tokens + llama_cpp.kv_elems_per_token * at(llama_cpp.kv_type_bytes, spend.kv_type) + (llama_cpp.kv_dequant_bytes if spend.kv_type in llama_cpp.kv_dequant_types else 0) + ((llama_cpp.draft_kv_elems_per_token * at(llama_cpp.kv_type_bytes, spend.kv_type_draft) + (llama_cpp.kpool_cell_bytes if llama_cpp.kpool_indexer else 2) * spend.draft_ubatch) if spend.draft_max > 0 else 0)
spend.cell_evidence: the 128k ledger's per-cell slopes (vram-ledger-20261118 section 2.1): main KV 13,056 + indexer keys 408 (mods 02-03 on) + masks 3.5 x -ub; draft KV 1,088 + masks 3.5 x its ubatch (measured 578 B a cell, 448 of it the masks; the other 128 and the draft's 34 B of indexer keys are not counted: 20 MiB at 128k)

rows.words: the sparse-attention layers' K/V kept whole in pinned host RAM, N cells a layer on the GPU (LLAMA_KV_STREAM=N)

needs.why: the mod pages the cache by 4 cells (its KVS_PAGE, the pool ratio it was written for) and this model pools {llama_cpp.kpool_ratio} cells a key: it is not built for that ratio

rows.valid: value == 'off' or (llama_cpp.kv_stream_layers > 0 and spend.kv_type == 'q8_0' and llama_cpp.kpool_ratio == 4 and value // 8 * 8 == value and value >= 4096 and value < context_tokens)

rows.bytes_why: each streamed layer keeps N of its context's cells on the GPU (pages), one staging pool holds a layer's K and V over the context, and each layer's page state is an int32 per page of the context and five per resident page ((context/4 + 5 x N/4) x 4 B: kv-stream.cu:868); fit_value: N is this machine's, the largest multiple of 8 (>= 4,096, below the context) the combination fits (8, not the mod's own 4: the mod takes any multiple of 4, but its page-resolve kernel keeps 64-bit counters after context/4 + 5 x N/4 int32 words (arkey_ie_mods 18351f1 kv.patch:+1054 on ctl() at +883), 8-byte aligned only when N/4 is even at a context that is a multiple of 8: N 65,292 and N 52,852 ended the server with a GPU exception as the context passed N, N 65,296 and N 52,848 ran (release-0331-20261120); the step stays 8 until the mod aligns them or refuses the N: b12521 aligns the control block from arkey_ie_mods 7f47bd2, the frozen 1.0.0 series does not), projected from the largest measured N at or below it (a larger N misses less: 128k N 32,768 cost -12.4 tok/s, N 65,536 -8.6); only_where_default_fails: on only where the same combination with it off does not fit (where it fits, paging frees memory nothing needs and costs decode time); limit: N leaves the runtime headroom a load-probe --stress measured (256k, N 32,768: +152 MiB beyond the session's lowest, a plateau in one round: kv-stream-20261118 kvs19), which assumes ggml-cuda's 10 s eviction of unused CUDA graphs and one client at a time (more clients or faster setting changes keep more graphs live); kv_stream_layers is 0 where the model has no sparse-attention layer with pooled keys, or the header lacks the rest of the shape the mod's own gate reads (data/mod_shapes.json kv-stream: head dims, query heads per K/V head, top-k; tune_llama_cpp.kv_stream_fit); 4 (the page, KVS_PAGE: kv-stream.cu) and 4,096 (the least N, kvs_check_n) are the mod's own constants, and the row is valid only at the pool ratio the page was written for; a row not built here is previewed at its least N, which frees the most; not modeled: the mod also needs one KV stream (n_stream 1) and the KV on the GPU; the mod ignores N >= the context, q8_0 K/V only, N a multiple of 4 and >= 4,096 (arkey_ie_mods llama.cpp 1.0.0 patch 20: llama-kv-stream.cpp kvs_check_n, plan, add_layer; kv-stream.cu:515-517, 534)
